abstracts.abstract: The escalating heterogeneity and geographic distribution of cloud workloads demand a fundamental reimagining of resource management paradigms. This paper introduces Federated Learning-Enabled Distributed Resource Orchestration (FL-DRO), a novel paradigm that shifts cloud resource management from centralized optimization to a collaborative, privacy-preserving distributed framework. Unlike traditional approaches that rely on global knowledge of system states, FL-DRO enables edge nodes and cloud datacenters to jointly optimize resource allocation while maintaining data locality. We formalize this paradigm through a multi-agent Markov decision process framework, where each node acts as an autonomous agent learning from local observations while contributing to a shared model through federated aggregation. Theoretical analysis proves the convergence bound of our approach under non-independent and identically distributed (non-IID) data distributions, demonstrating that FL-DRO achieves regret bounds of O(√T) compared to O(T) in traditional centralized methods. Furthermore, we establish the privacy-utility tradeoff bounds, proving that differential privacy guarantees can be maintained with minimal performance degradation. Simulation results across heterogeneous cloud-edge environments demonstrate that FL-DRO reduces task completion latency by 47% and improves energy efficiency by 38% compared to state-of-the-art centralized schedulers. This work fundamentally transforms how distributed cloud resources are managed, opening new research directions in decentralized cloud orchestration.

Efficient container scheduling in multi-cloud environments remains a critical challenge due to the complexity of optimizing across heterogeneous resource providers with conflicting objectives. This paper presents a novel mathematical framework for multi-objective container scheduling based on Constrained Markov Decision Processes (CMDP) with Lagrangian relaxation. Existing approaches typically address individual objectives in isolation or rely on heuristic methods that fail to capture the intricate dependencies between resource utilization, cost, and Quality of Service (QoS). Our framework unifies these objectives through a rigorously formulated constrained optimization problem, where container placement decisions are modeled as sequential actions in a stochastic environment. We develop a primal-dual policy gradient algorithm that simultaneously learns feasible scheduling policies while optimizing the Lagrangian multipliers for constraint satisfaction. Theoretical analysis establishes ε-feasibility and O(1/√T) convergence rates, providing rigorous guarantees that existing methods lack. Extensive trace-driven simulations using Google cluster workload traces demonstrate that our approach achieves 23% cost reduction compared to Kubernetes default scheduler while maintaining 99.9% SLA compliance. Compared to state-of-the-art deep reinforcement learning methods, our algorithm exhibits superior sample efficiency, requiring 65% fewer training episodes to achieve comparable performance. This work provides a theoretically grounded foundation for practical multi-cloud container orchestration.

The emergence of serverless computing and edge computing as complementary paradigms presents both opportunities and architectural challenges for cloud systems. This paper introduces ServerlessEdge, a novel system architecture that fundamentally unifies serverless function execution with edge computing infrastructure. Traditional approaches treat serverless platforms and edge systems as separate layers, requiring complex function partitioning and causing substantial cold-start delays for edge-deployed functions. ServerlessEdge eliminates this boundary through a hierarchical function lifecycle management system that dynamically migrates function execution between edge nodes and cloud datacenters based on real-time workload characteristics. The architecture incorporates a lightweight hypervisor layer enabling function checkpointing and rapid migration across heterogeneous edge devices, coupled with a distributed state management system maintaining consistent function state during migration. We implement a fully functional prototype integrating with OpenWhisk serverless platform and demonstrate its effectiveness across 50 edge nodes in a geo-distributed testbed. Evaluation results reveal that ServerlessEdge reduces function invocation latency by 58% compared to pure cloud serverless deployments while achieving 94% function migration success rate within 50ms. The system supports seamless state transfer for stateful functions, maintaining sub-100ms state recovery time. This architectural innovation redefines the relationship between serverless computing and edge infrastructure, enabling a new class of latency-sensitive cloud applications.

Container security in multi-cloud deployments remains a significant concern as organizations increasingly distribute applications across heterogeneous cloud providers with inconsistent security policies. This paper presents SecureMC, a comprehensive system for automated security policy enforcement and runtime threat detection in multi-cloud container environments. Existing solutions either rely on provider-specific security mechanisms lacking cross-platform consistency or employ heavyweight verification approaches incompatible with production deployment constraints. SecureMC introduces a policy specification language enabling unified security definitions portable across AWS, Azure, and GCP container services, coupled with a lightweight verification engine performing real-time compliance checking without significant performance overhead. The system incorporates novel runtime monitoring components that detect container escape attempts, privilege escalation, and anomalous network behavior through behavioral fingerprinting. We implement SecureMC as a Kubernetes operator framework with native integration into popular container runtimes. Evaluation across production workload traces demonstrates that SecureMC enforces security policies with 99.7% accuracy while introducing less than 3% latency overhead per container operation. The threat detection module achieves 96.3% true positive rate for known attack patterns in the CVEs dataset. Compared to existing multi-cloud security tools, SecureMC reduces security policy management effort by 71% through automated translation and enforcement. This work significantly advances practical security for multi-cloud container deployments.
